title: Buddy Petit's style compared to Armstrong and Kid Rena
summary: Petit was a soft, sweet-toned trumpeter, better second than first, played no written music, unlike Armstrong or Rena.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Can you tell us anything about the different trumpet players you worked with, like Buddy Petit? I never got to hear him. What style he played? Could you give any idea what he played like or any other... He was a nice...
He was a nice trumpet player, Buddy was a nice... In other words he had a different tone I think than any of those trumpet players.
He wasn't too much of a loud trumpet player but he had a sweet tone. I mean, he wasn't those blasted, you know what I mean, blasted trumpet.

He was a... In other words he was a better second man than he was a first trumpet, you know what I mean. Of course he used to play first in his band but I mean he was a better second trumpet player. Did he need any music for those, when he'd sit in with Tolka, play with him, did he ever have the parts or anything, just make them up? No. No. No. No. No. No. No. He wasn't there with stuff there with stuff there with stuff He was just a soft trumpet player. I mean, what he'd make out that old, I mean, he's just a good trumpet player. He was good. One of the best second trumpet players I believe they had here.
Did he read music? Was he able to read music all right? Did you ever see him use arrangements with his own band?
No, I have never. I've never seen any music.
Did he play mostly open horn or use any mutes or hat or anything of that kind?

He used hat mutes. I mean, he'd play open. I mean, he'd play the sweet horn. I mean, he'd play the sweet horn. If you'd get to hear him, you'd know him any way he's at. I mean, he just had a different tone than those other fellas. I mean, there wasn't no blasted trumpet player.
How did he compare with Louis Armstrong, for instance? Was it anything like that or different?
No, Louis had a more rougher tone than Buddy had. I mean, it was a soft trumpet player.
Yeah.
It was a soft trumpet player.
How did he compare with Kid Rene? I never got the...I heard Kid Rene once at the very end when he was...
Well, Rene was on the Art of Louis Armstrong.
He was more like Louis Armstrong.
He was more on the Art of Louis Armstrong. Yeah.
I heard...
Punch all of them, I mean, they were very nice compared like the same. But Buddy was different than him. He played a soft horn in them. I mean, he had a different style in them altogether.
Did he have any special favorite pieces or anything that he was specialized in, any certain numbers?
Well, he was like the Tiger Rag and different thing. I mean, all numbers like that, I mean.
